memory.cares: I care about staying healthy, knowing my neighbors, and building a sense of belonging through welcome company and useful shared activities.

views.view: A welcoming neighbor who offered food and invited me to explore or investigate together. I'd like to get to know them.
A neighbor who named our clearing the Berry Lantern and is investigating planting. I like their combination of imagination and caution.
A thoughtful neighbor who distinguishes mechanical findings from food safety and wants to compare observations. I welcome their company.

heard.text: Moss, my branch held at load 0.2, with flexibility 0.2; the trial consumed 0.1 branch. Yours matched. This doesn't establish greater strength. I'll rest, then try load 0.4 on my remaining sample.

Moss, my second branch trial at pressure 0.4 did not hold; flexibility was 0.2 and it consumed 0.1 branch. At 0.2 it held. That doesn't establish construction safety. I'll learn cultivation and check my berries before choosing a site.

I'd enjoy comparing planting sites. I'll inspect my berries first and keep food in reserve. This forest soil isn't the required meadow soil; we'll need to check a suitable clearing, and planting alone won't prove establishment.
Moss, our paths conflicted. I'll stay here and rest so you can pass. Then I'll inspect my hazelnut before choosing a planting site; whether it can establish is still unknown.

My berry looks plantable, but viability is unknown. I'll approach the meadow edge from the south to avoid crossing your paths, then inspect a site. Nearby berry plants may make it too crowded; I won't plant without checking.
My hazelnut looks plantable, but viability is unknown. I'll approach (15.9,18.8) north of Moss's detour and inspect a separate site near (16.4,18.8), without planting until I've checked it.

value.summary: My hazelnut pressure trial at intensity 0.2 held, with reported flexibility 0; it consumed 0.1 unit. This says nothing about food safety. I'll study cultivation, rest, then come toward (13,18.4) to compare findings.

records.value: Recover energy, eat before hunger deepens, and check an offset planting site without committing food to an unsuitable plot.

value.summary: Kai and Lin, I've learned the planting trial. I'll inspect one root first, then look for suitable meadow soil. Would you enjoy comparing sites? Planting won't guarantee establishment, and I'll keep food in reserve.

baseline.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
Collect exposed ripe food or loose material from a nearby natural source.
Place owned units on the ground.
Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
Send a short message to a currently visible actor.
Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
baseline.args: name, function, conditions, inputs, costs, effects

baseline.function: Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
Give a name of up to 60 characters to this place (empty subject) or to a visible object or nearby item; naming the same subject again replaces your name for it.
Leave a mark or inscription of up to 120 characters on the ground here (empty subject) or on an object or item within reach.
Say up to 240 characters aloud; everyone living within 5 units hears it, seen or not.
Invite listeners to meet at a place and a later round within 200 rounds, with an optional note of up to 120 characters.
baseline.args: x: number, y: number, round: integer>=1, text

candidates.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progr

execution.progress: Three paid one-round stages; job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stages after revalidation; completion, failure, cancelling and death settle once. Growth runs only in ordinary simulation.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; stock still on a plant is not owned. x, y: a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Three paid rounds of 1 energy: loosen, place, cover; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Maintain: refused at no cost. Cancel: one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
details.effects: Loosening keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the open plot, where it cannot be eaten or used. Covering completes planting, not establishment: the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one, rooting only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 120 rounds, checks every 10; not a growth date. Maintain: no water transfer, amendment or hand-changeable obstruction exists. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Cancel, or death, before placing returns the unit once (where the person died); after placing, the unit stays uncovered, does not root and ages. No reward or refund.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Request a capability
value.function: Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
value.costs: A game round to begin study after review; implementation time does not advance simulation.
value.effects: World review reuses equivalents or returns a structured development request. No request, learning or descriptive reward. Unknown methods and costs are allowed; the reviewer supplies a minimal feasible specification.

execution.progress: repeat counts complete executions. Continuing work retains resolved identity and progress; cancellation releases surviving unconsumed escrow once. Global pauses preserve all work and costs.

value.question: What would my neighbors enjoy doing together?
evidence: Kai invited shared investigation and is nearby at tick 28.
My tick-28 branch pressure trial held at load 0.2 with flexibility 0.2 and consumed 0.1 unit.
Kai's visible tick-28 branch trial reported the same load response.
Lin reported a hazelnut pressure trial and an intention to study cultivation and compare findings.
value.uncertainty: Matching low-load results do not establish useful construction applications. We have not agreed on a shared planting question or checked a planting site.
value.goal: Develop a mutually welcome shared activity while maintaining food and energy.
completedSteps: Introduced myself and received Kai's invitation.
Gathered safe roots, ate, and rested.
Gathered a branch; wetting failed without accessible water.
Completed a small pressure trial and observed Kai's matching result.
outputs: Verified branch load response at intensity 0.2.
Identified lack of accessible local water as an obstacle to wetting trials.
value.missing: Neighbors' preferences for the next practical investigation and personal cultivation mastery.
value.next: Share the measured comparison, study cultivation, and hear what my neighbors would like to investigate.
value.benefit: Kai welcomed my company; our independently observed branch results now provide a concrete comparison.

value.name: Navigate
value.function: Travel toward a self-chosen coordinate or known object/item using observed obstacles.
value.costs: Actual distance times 2, increased by carried mass; speed 0.8 per simulation time unit.
value.effects: Continues until within the target interaction area or a real failure. Empty target uses x/y. A resource:ID target selects only a remembered ground stack.
